llmPrompt:
This is a Scratch program called "has.sb3".
It has 16 sprites: Loop, Menu, Messages, Stats, Level, Background, Spawn, Spots, Path, Level Editor, Player, Bot1, Bot2, Bot3, Bot4, Thumbnail.
It uses a virtual camera system (variables: ZOOM, CAM X, CAM Y). Sprites are intentionally moved off the 480×360 stage as the camera pans — spatial bounds violations are expected and are NOT bugs.
The game tracks state using: "CURRENT PLAYER STAT" (current value: "hided"), "MENU" (current value: "In-Game").
Score/stat variables (should only increase): Highest rescue streak:, Total Players found:, Your total rescues:, Rescue streak:, Meters walked:, Stealth meters:, point of intrest, at point of intrest?, point of intrest, at point of intrest?, point of intrest, at point of intrest?, point of intrest, at point of intrest?, point of intrest, at point of intrest?, point of intrest, at point of intrest?.
WARNING: 14 variable IDs are shared across multiple sprites. This means writes to those variables in one sprite immediately affect another sprite — a likely aliasing bug.
Inferred game states: Boot → Initialising → Menu → Playing → GameOver.
Tick broadcasts (fire every frame): Level Editor - Tick, Level - Tick, Spots - Tick, Bot1 - Tick, LevelHitbox - Tick, Player - Tick, Visiblity - Tick, Bot2 - Tick, Bot3 - Tick, Bot4 - Tick, Path - Tick, Stats - Tick, Tutorial - Tick.
End-of-round broadcasts: End Game-Round.
Sprites with collision detection logic: Menu, Level, Spawn, Spots, Path, Player, Bot1, Bot2, Bot3, Bot4.

Based on the above, list 5 to 8 properties that should ALWAYS be true while this program runs. For each property, write it as a single sentence starting with "The". Focus on game logic correctness, not graphical rendering.
